q: 1. Working/ drawing space on the paper is determined by
explain: Border lines are drawn on the sheet to define the actual area available for the technical drawing and to provide a frame for the work.

q: 2. Which of the following is preferred containing the statement "All dimensions are in millimeters unless otherwise specified" .............
explain: General notes such as the units statement are conventionally placed within the title block of the drawing sheet.

q: 3. Size of A4 size paper is
explain: A4 is the most common paper size, measuring exactly 210mm by 297mm.

q: 4. "A" series of paper has length of width ratio of approximately .............
explain: ISO A-series paper sizes maintain a constant aspect ratio of √2:1, which allows each size to be halved into the next smaller size while preserving the same proportions.

q: 5. Number of equal pieces of A4 size paper from A0 is equal to
explain: Each step in the A-series halves the area. $A0 \rightarrow A1 \rightarrow A2 \rightarrow A3 \rightarrow A4$. That is $2^4 = 16$ sheets.

q: 6. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A1 (drawing sheet).
explain: One A0 sheet is equivalent to two A1 sheets placed side-by-side.

q: 7. The area occupied by A0 (drawing sheet) is ............ times the area occupied by A3 (drawing sheet).
explain: Following the division rule ($2^3$), A0 is eight times the size of A3.

q: 8. During draw a drawing we start from
options: top to bottom of drawing paper
bottom to top of drawing paper
right to left of drawing paper
left to right of drawing paper
explain: Drawing from top-to-bottom and left-to-right (for right-handed users) prevents the hand or tools from smudging lines that were already drawn.

q: 9. The size of title block of all size drawing sheet is
explain: As per standard drafting practice, the title block occupies a fixed area of 185 mm × 65 mm regardless of sheet size.

q: 10. The ratio of distance on the drawing sheet and corresponding actual distance of the object is known as
explain: This ratio, drawing distance to actual distance, is by definition called the Representative Factor (RF).

q: 11. Which of the following is the largest size of a engineering drawing sheet?
explain: In the ISO A-series, the sheet number decreases as size increases; A0 (841×1189 mm) is the largest of the options listed.

q: 12. Tracing paper is also named as .............
explain: Tracing paper used in drafting is also generically referred to as drafting media, a term covering various transparent/translucent sheet materials used for tracing drawings.

q: 13. In standard A series drawing sheet, the ratio of length of shorter side to longer side is equal to:
explain: The A-series sheets maintain a constant aspect ratio of shorter side to longer side equal to 1:√2.

q: 14. The measurement of standard A2 size drawing sheet in mm is .............
explain: Standard ISO A2 sheet size is 420 mm × 594 mm, consistent with the halving pattern of the A-series from A0 downward.

q: 15. The included angle of a pentagon is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, option (b) 72° is marked correct; this corresponds to the central (apex) angle of a regular pentagon when divided into 5 equal triangles from its center (360°/5 = 72°), while the interior angle of a pentagon is actually 108°.

q: 16. "Title Block" is placed at bottom right hand corner of the drawing which gives information about
explain: The title block is the metadata center of a drawing, containing names, dates, scales, and identification numbers.

q: 17. *In standard A series drawing sheet, the ratio of length of shorter side to longer side
explain: ISO 216 standard (A series) uses a constant aspect ratio of 1 to the square root of 2 ($1:\sqrt{2}$) so that the proportions remain the same when the sheet is folded in half.

q: 18. The best drawing paper used for water colour is :
explain: Though handmade paper is traditionally used, the answer key specifies tracing/technical sheets in this specific engineering context.

q: 19. The size of the title block of all sizes of drawing sheet is :
explain: According to Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), the standard size for a title block is 185 mm x 65 mm.

q: 20. The normal size of drawing sheet referred as 'A1' is:
explain: As per ISO A-series, A1 measures 594 mm × 841 mm.

q: 21. *Working drawings:
options: must provide complete information to produce the object
should be supplemented by further details
explain: A working drawing must contain all necessary dimensions, notes, and views for a manufacturer to build the part without further questions.

q: 22. The point of intersection of co-ordinate axis is called .............
explain: The point where the coordinate axes (X, Y, Z) intersect, representing the reference point (0,0,0), is universally called the origin.

q: 23. Church in a drawing sheet is symbolized as:
explain: On maps/plans, a church is conventionally shown as a small figure/symbol (often a cross-topped icon) rather than a plain point.

q: 24. The paper size of A4 is (in mm)
explain: As per ISO A-series, A4 measures 210 mm × 297 mm.

q: 25. The ISO A0 size of drawing is defined as having an area of .............
explain: The ISO A0 sheet size is defined such that its area equals exactly 1 square meter, from which all other A-series sizes are derived by successive halving.

q: 26. The paper size of A4 is .............
explain: The standard ISO A4 paper size is 210 mm × 297 mm, the most commonly used sheet size for general documents and smaller drawings.

q: 27. Working drawings are prepared at the stage of .............
explain: Working drawings, containing full dimensions and construction details, are produced during the detail design stage, after the concept has been finalized and before construction execution.

q: 28. The size of drawing board required for A0 sheet size in mm is .............
explain: To accommodate an A0 sheet (841×1189 mm) with margins for pinning and T-square movement, a larger drawing board of approximately 1500×1000×25 mm is required.
